claims.claim: The person registering the death must be a qualified informant.
claims.quote: the giving of information and the signing of the register by any one qualified informant shall act as a discharge of any duty under this subsection of every other qualified informant
claims.note: The Births and Deaths Registration Act sets out who is qualified to give information and that a qualified informant gives the information and signs the register.

claims.claim: A relative can be a qualified informant.
claims.quote: A relative should usually register the death.
claims.note: Citizens Advice (England) says a relative should usually register the death; the Act lists relatives present at the death, in attendance during the last illness or living in the sub-district.

claims.claim: Someone present at the death can be a qualified informant.
claims.quote: (c) any person present at the death;
claims.note: The Act lists any person present at the death as qualified to give information.

claims.claim: An administrator of the premises where the death happened can be a qualified informant.
claims.quote: (d) the occupier of the house if he knew of the happening of the death;
claims.note: The Act names the occupier of the house (if they knew of the death), not an administrator of the premises; only a single council page equates occupier with an establishment's manager or senior administrator.

claims.claim: Registering the death is required for every death in England and Wales.
claims.quote: It’s a criminal offence not to register a death.
claims.note: The source says it is a criminal offence not to register a death, but this advice is stated for England; the sources do not state the requirement for every death in Wales in the same terms.

claims.claim: Registration must be done by a qualified informant such as a relative or a person present at the death.
claims.quote: the giving of information and the signing of the register by any one qualified informant shall act as a discharge of any duty under this subsection of every other qualified informant
claims.note: The Act places the duty to register on qualified informants, who include relatives and persons present at the death.

claims.claim: The death must be registered within 5 days.
claims.quote: Register the death within 5 days (8 days in Scotland) of getting the confirmation.
claims.note: GOV.UK says to register within 5 days of the medical examiner's office confirming you can register.
